messages.author: 99ee8dd46d28d73c
messages.subject: random walk model
parts:
Hi all,

I encountered a problem with the RW1 model in INLA and hope anyone can offer some suggestions:

I have the following small experiment in R:

#function to generate RW 
RW <- function(N, x0, mu, variance) {
  z<-cumsum(rnorm(n=N, mean=0,
                  sd=sqrt(variance)))
  t<-1:N
  x<-x0+t*mu+z
  return(x)
}

b1 <-sample(c(0:1),size=N, replace=TRUE)
theta <- 0.75
idx <- ifelse(trt==0, 0, sample(c(0:12), size=length(b1==1),  replace = TRUE))

RW_theta <- RW(13, 0, 0.75/13, 0)
error <- rnorm(N,0,1.6)

y <-  b1*(theta + RW_theta[idx+1]) + error
data <- data.frame(y=y, b1=b1, idx=idx, ID=ID, error=error)

lc1 <- inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(-1,rep(NA,13-2),1))

test.rw1 <- inla(y ~ b1 + f(idx, b1, model="rw1"),
                 control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param = c(10, 10)))),
                 data= data,
                 lincomb = lc1,
                 control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), family = "gaussian")


I am interested in the posterior distribution of idx[12]-idx[1], so I have the above linear comb defined. However, for some reasons, the posterior means of random effects for idx are all close to zero (see the picture below); therefore, the linear combination is also close to zero. This is confusing as I would expect it to be 0.75/13*12=0.69 (0.75/13 is the drift of the RW). Also, the mean of the posterior distribution for b1 is 0.412. This value does not make sense, and I expect this to be "theta + the center of the RW".

Did I do anything wrong??

Best,
Derek

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random walk model
parts:
the code is incomplete so I cannot rerun it here

the prior says the mean of the RW is 0, and then also the mean of differences.
additionally, there implicite a sum-to-zero constraint that amplifies this.

You have a very complex model for N=13 datapoints, and you would need a higher N
to justify your claim. Also, the model allows for different interpretations and
you need the prior to say which one you like (or which ones you do not want)

H

Dear  Håvard,

Thanks for the reply. I apologize for the incomplete code. I have included an updated one in this post. 
I have been trying different priors, but it has a limited impact on the RW model. For example, the following one shows a normal prior with a non-zeon mean.
I would be really appreciated if you could explain a bit more about "Also, the model allows for different interpretations, and you need the prior to say which one you like (or which ones you do not want)"
My goal is to estimate the drift of the RW model.

Many thanks,
Derek

library(INLA)
set.seed(123)
RW <- function(n, x0, mu, variance) {
  z<-cumsum(rnorm(n=n, mean=0,
                  sd=sqrt(variance)))
  t<-1:n
  x<-x0+t*mu+z
  return(x)
}
# number of individuals in the dataset
N = 200

lc1 <- inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(-1,rep(NA,13-2),1))

test.rw1 <- inla(y ~ b1 + f(idx, b1, model="rw1"),

data= data,
                 lincomb = lc1,
                 control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE), family = "gaussian")

RW(N, 0, 0, 0.75/13)

parameters you used to simulated with.

at least you can start from there.

unless you have the constr=T in the rw1, there is a confounding with 'theta'

hope this helps
H
